items.item: Workshop on young people staying in or leaving Wausau
items.why: Council members will meet with student representatives to discuss issues affecting young people and their decisions about living in Wausau.

items.item: Student and group priorities from the workshop
items.why: The council will discuss and possibly act on priorities identified by students and groups during the workshop.

preview.overview: The Wausau Common Council is scheduled to hold a workshop with student representatives to discuss why young people leave, return to, or stay in Wausau. The council will discuss and may act on student and group priorities that come out of the workshop.

items.item: Seven 2027 budgets for housing programs and facilities
items.why: The board is asked to vote on separate budgets for the Housing Choice Voucher Program, Public Housing Program, Riverview Terrace, Riverview Towers LLC, Fulton Street, and 8th Avenue.

items.item: Repositioning public housing scattered sites to voucher program
items.why: The board is asked to vote on Resolution #26-012 to convert scattered public housing sites to project-based vouchers after a consultant presents repositioning options.

items.item: Riverview Towers façade repair bids
items.why: The board is asked to discuss and vote on bids received for masonry and concrete façade repairs at Riverview Towers LLC.

items.item: Sub-recipient agreement for 405 S 8th Avenue property
items.why: The board is asked to discuss and vote on a rental property agreement between the city and the authority for 405 S 8th Avenue.

items.item: Capital needs assessment for scattered sites properties
items.why: The board is asked to discuss and vote on a request for proposals for a capital needs assessment of scattered public housing sites.

items.item: Presentation on repositioning options for scattered sites
items.why: S.C. Koegler Consulting will present comprehensive repositioning options for the authority's scattered public housing sites.

preview.overview: The Community Development Authority is scheduled to vote on seven budgets for housing programs and facilities. The board will also consider reshaping its public housing scattered sites program and approve repair bids for Riverview Towers.

items.item: EPA technical assistance for 1300 Cleveland Avenue redevelopment
items.why: The committee is asked to approve a scope of work for EPA OBLR (Brownfields) Land Revitalization Technical Assistance providing site visioning and financing support for 1300 Cleveland Avenue.

items.item: Update on 1019 West Bridge Street infill housing project
items.why: The committee will receive an update on infill housing development at 1019 West Bridge Street.

preview.overview: The Economic Development Committee is scheduled to approve federal technical assistance for a brownfield redevelopment project at 1300 Cleveland Avenue. The committee will also hear an update on infill housing development at 1019 West Bridge Street.

items.item: Student expulsion hearing
items.why: The board will hold a closed hearing to consider expulsion of a student under Wisconsin law.

preview.overview: The Mosinee School Board is scheduled to hold a closed student expulsion hearing. The board will meet in private session under state law to conduct the hearing.

items.item: PFAS settlement funds for capital projects
items.why: The commission is scheduled to vote on approving how to use settlement money for water system improvements.

items.item: Lead service line replacement fund borrowing
items.why: The commission is scheduled to vote on borrowing money from the regular drinking water funding program to replace lead service lines on the public side of connections.

items.item: Lead and Copper Rule revisions and improvements
items.why: The director will report on new federal rules for lead and copper in drinking water and what they mean for Wausau.

items.item: Water service line replacement plan
items.why: The director will report on Wausau's plan to replace water service lines, developed with engineering firm Jacobs Engineering.

items.item: 2026 sanitary survey
items.why: The director will report on the annual drinking water safety inspection and testing results.

items.item: Carbon regeneration of water treatment vessels
items.why: The commission is scheduled to vote on approving Carbon Activated Corporation to regenerate six more activated carbon vessels used to treat drinking water.

preview.overview: The Water Works Commission is scheduled to review drinking water safety reports and decide how to spend settlement funds for water infrastructure projects. The commission will also discuss plans to replace lead service lines in Wausau.

items.item: Interview candidates for Wausau Police Department Deputy Chief
items.why: The commission will meet in closed session to interview two candidates for the Deputy Chief position and may vote on a hiring decision in open session afterward.

preview.overview: The Police & Fire Commission is scheduled to interview two candidates for Deputy Chief with the Wausau Police Department in a closed session on December 2.

items.item: 2026 budget modification for year-end projections
items.why: The Finance Committee is asking the council to approve various budget adjustments based on how the year ended.

items.item: Salary structure revision for general city employees
items.why: The Finance Committee and Human Resources Committee are asking the council to revise how general employees' salaries are structured.

items.item: Special assessments for 2027 street construction projects
items.why: The Infrastructure & Facilities Committee is asking the council to levy special assessments (charges to property owners) to pay for street work in 2027.

items.item: Deed restrictions and non-conforming uses at 1300 Cleveland Avenue
items.why: The Economic Development Committee is asking the council to approve deed restrictions and clarify existing non-conforming uses on city-owned property.

items.item: Driveway and concrete approach exceptions for Kolbe & Kolbe Millwork
items.why: The Infrastructure & Facilities Committee is asking the council to approve oversized driveways and waive a concrete approach requirement at three nearby addresses on South 11th Avenue.

items.item: District 9 aldermanic vacancy
items.why: The Common Council is addressing how to fill an empty aldermanic seat in District 9.

preview.overview: The Common Council will vote on the 2026 budget modification and several resolutions affecting city property and employee pay. The council will also meet in closed session to discuss litigation strategy.

items.item: Policy 2240.01 - Classroom Displays
items.why: The board will discuss and may vote on a new policy governing what can be displayed in school classrooms.

items.item: Fund 80 Levy and Expenditures
items.why: The board will discuss Fund 80, which is a special school funding account, and how those dollars are spent.

items.item: Mosinee School District Day Care
items.why: The board will discuss the district's day care services and operations.

items.item: Board Member Communication with Administration
items.why: The board will discuss how members should communicate with school administrators.

items.item: Board Agenda Planning
items.why: The board will discuss and may vote on how to plan future meeting agendas.

preview.overview: The Mosinee School Board is scheduled to discuss classroom display policies and school day care services. The board will also hold a closed session to discuss personnel matters.

items.item: Approving title for Five-Year Sustainability Plan
items.why: The committee will vote on a name for the city's comprehensive five-year sustainability plan.

items.item: Five-Year Sustainability Plan and Work Plan Strategy
items.why: The committee will discuss the draft Five-Year Sustainability Plan and Five-Year Work Plan Strategy.

items.item: Community and Business Sustainability Survey results
items.why: The committee will discuss results from surveys about sustainability sent to the community and local businesses.

items.item: Earth Week Community Pollinator Garden Public Art Proposal
items.why: The committee will receive an update on a public art proposal for a pollinator garden tied to Earth Week.

items.item: Wausau Sustainability Award
items.why: The committee will receive an update on the Wausau Sustainability Award.

preview.overview: The Sustainability, Energy & Environment Committee will vote on a title for the city's Five-Year Sustainability Plan. The committee will also discuss survey results and review draft plans for the city's sustainability work over the next five years.

items.item: Enforcement of historic property maintenance requirements
items.why: The commission will discuss how to enforce rules that require owners of historic properties to maintain them properly.

items.item: Historic district signs: quantity, cost, and funding
items.why: The commission will discuss and decide on the number, cost, and funding for signs marking historic districts in Wausau.

items.item: Historic Preservation Commission webpage
items.why: The commission will discuss and vote on creating a webpage to inform residents and historic property owners about preservation rules and information.

items.item: Future landmarks for consideration
items.why: The commission will discuss which Wausau buildings or sites might become historic landmarks in the future.

preview.overview: The Historic Preservation Commission will discuss how to enforce maintenance rules for historic properties and consider new signs for historic districts. The commission will also vote on creating a website to inform residents about historic preservation.

items.item: Recommendation for 2026 demolition of 207 North 1st Avenue
items.why: The board will decide whether to recommend demolition of the building at 207 North 1st Avenue (MBX South). Bids were opened on November 17.

items.item: Pay estimates for lift station and street projects
items.why: The board will approve four contractor payments: a second payment for Crocker Street Lift Station work, final payment for Cherry Street Lift Station, first payment for downtown sidewalk improvements, and final payment for asphalt paving project.

preview.overview: The Board of Public Works is scheduled to decide whether to recommend demolition of a building at 207 North 1st Avenue. The board will also approve payments for several street and utility projects around the city.

hearings: Amendment to Ordinance §17.08-5: Accessory Uses and Structures
Amendment to Ordinance §17.13: Principal Building Lot Coverage

items.item: Amendment to Ordinance §17.08-5: Accessory Uses and Structures
items.why: The commission will hear public comments on proposed changes to rules governing accessory structures, then vote on whether to approve the amendment.

items.item: Amendment to Ordinance §17.13: Principal Building Lot Coverage
items.why: The commission will hear public comments on proposed changes to rules about how much of a lot a main building can occupy, then vote on whether to approve the amendment.

preview.overview: The Plan Commission is scheduled to hold two public hearings on changes to village zoning rules. Residents can comment on proposed changes to rules about accessory structures and building lot coverage.

items.item: Animal impoundment services agreement with Humane Society
items.why: The committee will vote to approve a contract with the Humane Society of Marathon County for the city to use their animal impoundment services.

items.item: Five other service and equipment purchase agreements
items.why: The committee will vote to approve agreements for mapping software (Esri), county production services, cemetery operations, and fire department cardiac monitors and ventilators.

items.item: Budget change and lift purchase for Athletic Park
items.why: The committee will vote to approve a budget modification and sole source request to buy an outdoor vertical platform lift for Athletic Park.

items.item: Update on county pet license fee changes for 2027
items.why: City staff will update the committee on how Marathon County plans to change pet license fees starting in 2027.

preview.overview: The Finance Committee is scheduled to vote on six agreements and contracts for city services. These include animal impounding, mapping software, cemetery operations, and fire department equipment purchases.

items.item: Executive Director's Report
items.why: The board will discuss and possibly act on matters in the executive director's report, though specific topics are not detailed on the agenda.

preview.overview: The Business Improvement District Board will meet to review past meeting minutes and hear an executive director's report. The agenda does not list specific decisions or hearings for residents.

items.item: Interview and wages for part-time treasurer/deputy clerk
items.why: The board will meet in closed session to interview candidates and set the wage for this part-time position.

items.item: Wage for part-time snowplow driver
items.why: The board will meet in closed session to set the wage for this part-time position.

preview.overview: The Village of Maine board is scheduled to meet in private to discuss hiring and pay for two village positions: a part-time treasurer/deputy clerk and a part-time snowplow driver.
